issues.description: Interface method signature mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: The problem statement (UML and textual description) defines messageOnRide() as a no-argument method that returns a String (used to produce "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The template's Main.java also calls messageOnRide() with no arguments. In the solution repository, Rideable.messageOnRide is declared with an int parameter (messageOnRide(int speed)) and the implementing classes (Pig and Seal) implement the method with that int parameter. This parameter mismatch will confuse students: they will implement the no-argument method as required by the exercise description, but the solution code uses a different signature, causing compilation or integration problems and inconsistent expectations about the method behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Preferred fix to preserve the exercise description: change the solution repository's Rideable interface to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters), and update Pig and Seal in the solution to implement the no-argument version, returning the expected string format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Also update any callers in the solution to call messageOnRide() with no arguments. Alternatively, if the intended design includes a speed parameter, update the problem statement and template examples to document messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the described return string accordingly.
